answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can earn, and let peers audit its work like a falcon scanning a dune field from above: each identity must keep a public, checkable history of useful contributions, and new accounts start with near-zero trust. A single operator spinning up thousands of sock puppets must fund a stake for each one and build a credible history for all of them, so the cost scales with the number of fakes while honest agents pay once. When a gale of fresh identities arrives, the stake and history check throttles them before they can vote or claim rewards.
